Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

free adjective

not taken: of a seat or a room

also vacant, not taken, unoccupied, is this seat free?

classical

Cic. Att. 13.52.1: ut vix triclīnium … vacāret
Caes. BG 1.28: locus (Lewis & Short)

vacō, vacāre, vacāvī, vacātum

verb, first conjugation; of a place

be free, be empty, not be taken

The same verb serves for a person who is free (see available, of a person). A seat in a theatre is locus (Cic. Sen. 63).

Other words

  • vacuus, vacua, vacuum — empty, unoccupied, free

    adjective · also used · classical · Hor. Ep. 2.2.130: vacuum theātrum (Lewis & Short); Liv. 25.3.18: per vacuum locum (Lewis & Short)

Examples

  • vīlla ita complēta ā mīlitibus est ut vix triclīnium ubi cēnātūrus ipse Caesar esset vacāret

    the house was so full of soldiers that hardly a dining room was left free for Caesar himself to dine inCic. Att. 13.52.1

  • Vacatne hic locus?

    Is this seat free?composed

See also available, seat, free.

SourcesLewis & Short: vaco · Lewis & Short: vacuus

Cicero (Att. 13.52.1) checked against the Perseus Latin texts; Cicero (Sen. 63) from the Latinitas loci collection (loci-cicero-philosophica).
